Swear is about speaking with the strongest possible weight behind your words — whether that means binding yourself to a promise, expressing strong emotion, or firmly claiming something is true.

It has three distinct main meanings, plus a few important phrase-based uses.
Meaning 1: To Make a Solemn, Formal Promise

This is the oldest and most serious use of the word. When you swear, you make a promise so strong and serious that it is treated as absolutely binding — often before a court, a god, or a formal authority. The promise isn't casual; it carries real moral or legal weight.

"I swear to tell the truth."
"She swore an oath of loyalty to the country."
"He swore on his mother's life that he didn't do it."

The key idea here is commitment. A swear in this sense is not like saying "I promise" lightly to a friend. It is a declaration that you are fully, seriously bound to what you say.

Related phrase — "swear in" / "be sworn in": When someone officially takes on an important position (like a president, a judge, or a witness in court), they publicly make this kind of oath, and we say they are sworn in.

"The new president was sworn in on January 20th."
"The witness was sworn in before giving testimony."
Meaning 2: To Use Offensive or Profane Language (Cursing)

This is the everyday, informal meaning most people are familiar with. When someone swears, they say words that are considered rude, offensive, or socially inappropriate — what are commonly called swear words, curse words, or bad language.

"Please don't swear in front of the children."
"He swore loudly when he hit his toe on the table."
"She rarely swears, even when she's very angry."

The connection between this meaning and Meaning 1 is historical: in earlier times, saying God's name or invoking sacred things casually or disrespectfully was considered a terrible misuse of oaths. Over time, this gave rise to the idea of "swearing" as using forbidden or shocking language.
Meaning 3: To Firmly and Confidently Declare Something Is True

Here, you are not making a promise about the future, and you're not using bad language. Instead, you are insisting very strongly that something is or was true, often to convince someone who might be doubtful.

"I swear I locked the door before we left."
"She swears she saw a UFO last night."
"I could have sworn I left my phone on the table." (= I am almost certain, even if it turned out to be wrong)

Notice the phrase "could have sworn" — it's used when you were very sure about something, but it turned out you might have been mistaken. It expresses strong but ultimately uncertain confidence.

▸ Swear by (something)

To trust something completely and enthusiastically recommend it based on your own experience.

"My grandmother swears by honey and lemon for a sore throat."
"He swears by this brand of running shoes."

▸ Swear off (something)

To firmly promise yourself that you will stop doing or having something, usually because it has caused you harm.

"After years of smoking, she finally swore off cigarettes."
"He swore off social media after it started affecting his mood."

"Swear" is an irregular verb, which means it does not follow the normal "-ed" pattern.

  • Present: swear / swears
  • Past tense: swore
  • Past participle (used with have/has/had or in passive constructions): sworn

"She swore she'd never do it again." (past)
"He has sworn to protect the city." (past participle)
"They took a sworn statement." (adjective use of past participle)
How to Tell Which Meaning Is Being Used

Context almost always makes it clear:

  • If someone is in a courtroom, a ceremony, or promising something gravely → Meaning 1 (oath/solemn promise).
  • If someone is expressing frustration with colorful language → Meaning 2 (profanity).
  • If someone is insisting a personal claim is true → Meaning 3 (strong assertion).
A Few Natural, Everyday Examples Putting It All Together

• "I swear I'm telling the truth." → Asserting sincerity (Meaning 3)
  • "He swore at the referee after the bad call." → Used offensive language (Meaning 2)
  • "She was sworn in as the new governor this morning." → Took a formal oath (Meaning 1)
  • "I swear by cold showers — they wake you up instantly." → Trusts it completely (phrasal verb)
  • "He swore off fast food after his doctor's visit." → Promised to quit (phrasal verb)
The One Thing That Ties All Meanings Together

No matter which sense you use "swear" in, the word always carries an idea of intensity and weight. You don't swear about small, trivial things. Whether it's a legal oath, a strong claim, or even a curse word — "swear" signals that something forceful and serious is being expressed.
